facts.fact: Law 2020-34 of 6 January 2021 dematerialised civil status and abolished paper civil registers, so every birth is registered in the RNPP, which counts as the civil-status declaration, per ANIP.
facts.system: RNPP / Fichier National de l'Etat Civil

facts.fact: ANIP says a death updates the person's status in the RNPP automatically and law 2020-34 allows late registration of deaths of people enrolled in the RNPP.
facts.system: RNPP / Fichier National de l'Etat Civil

facts.fact: ANIP says it is in charge of the electoral file and that the electoral list is available in a few clicks.
ANIP says its USSD channel is used massively for consulting and transferring electors.
ANIP says a death recorded in the RNPP automatically removes the person from the electoral lists.
ANIP says nearly 13.8 million people are enrolled in the RNPP, the national population register, as at 6 May 2026.
ANIP says a birth declaration enters the person in the RNPP and a death automatically updates the RNPP.
ANIP says the RNPP is the only source for identity cards, passports and driving licences, and that phone SIM acquisition and public service platforms authenticate against the NPI.
